title: Model again when the genre changes
statement: When the genre changes or texts get harder, model a strategy again with coached practice before independent use, rather than assuming what was learned on stories carries over.
detail: An IES video on the gradual release of responsibility, quoted in a reading course's review standard, says the model is gone through back and forth many times and that a new genre may mean starting again with more of the responsibility on the teaching side (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/teaching-moves/gradual-release-as-a-loop.md`). It places growth in the coached middle, where the student applies the strategy with plenty of guidance, and calls the big leap from explicit teaching straight to independent use the habit of less effective teaching. A second video, on informational text, asks for instruction in narrative and informational texts kept separate and very clear. The standard therefore tracks a strategy's release for each genre and difficulty band, not once for all texts.

evidence.quote: if we introduce a new genre, we may need to start back up with the teacher having more responsibility.
less effective teachers will often make a big leap in their strategy instruction. They'll explicitly teach a strategy, and then they send kids off to use it on their own.
We go back and forth through this model many times.
And then the important middle is where the student is applying it, but the teacher is still there giving lots of support, lots of guidance, lots of coaching.
you really need to give students instruction in narrative and in informational texts, and those really have to be separate and very, very clear.
A strategy's release state is tracked *per genre/difficulty band*, not globally.
